want.now.why: No 'I': the a- prefix on أريد and أتعلم marks the speaker. أن (an) links the two verbs, like English 'to'.

want.past.why: Past goes on a separate كنت (kuntu, 'I was') while أريد stays present; أردت (aradtu) also works but sounds more one-off.

want.neg.why: لا (laa) goes straight before the present verb with no 'do'. Levantine swaps it for ما: ما بدّي إتعلّم (ma baddi et3allam).

want.q.why: هل (hal) at the front makes it a yes/no question and nothing moves. 'You' is only the t- prefix on تريد and تتعلم.

decline.now.why: HAVE-TO is عليّ (3alayya, 'on me'): a preposition with the person built in, like Hindi मुझे. Both subjects are dropped.

decline.past.why: Past sits in the negator: لم (lam) plus a non-past verb means 'didn't'. عليّ has no tense, so كان (kaana) is added.

decline.fut.why: لن (lan) is a separate negator just for the future: laa for now, lam for the past, lan for later. سيكون puts عليّ into the future.

decline.although.why: Same shape as the because sentence, with مع أن (ma3a anna, literally 'with that') in place of لأن.

like.now.why: Plain verb then object, and the pronoun is dropped. Levantine adds a b- prefix: بحبّ القهوة (b7ebb il-2ahwe).

like.neg.why: Only لا (laa) is added in front. The verb does not change and there is no 'do'.

like.she.why: تحب (tu7ibb) is spelled exactly like 'you (m.) like', so هي (hiya, she) is kept to show who. Only the prefix changes, a- to t-.

like.q.why: هل plus the plain statement. In Levantine speech people drop هل and ask with rising pitch: بتحبّ القهوة؟

go.habit.why: Verb first with the pronoun dropped, then place, then time. Levantine uses a different verb: بروح عالسوق (bruu7 3as-suu2).

go.prog.why: No word for 'am'. أنا plus the participle ذاهب ('going', an adjective-like form) is a full sentence. Levantine: أنا رايح.

go.past.why: ذهبت is a different verb shape: the -tu suffix carries both 'I' and the past, where the present used an a- prefix.

go.fut.why: 'Will' is the prefix sa- written onto أذهب as one word; سوف أذهب is the separate-word version. Levantine: رح روح (ra7 ruu7).

go.neg.why: لست (lastu, 'I am not') is a negator that takes a person ending. The participle then takes the -an ending: ذاهبًا.

live.now.why: Plain present with منذ (mundhu, since) does the 'have been' work. سنتين is the dual form: 'two years' in one word.

live.past.why: The past verb سكنت (sakantu) closes the time span. لمدة (li-muddat, 'for a period of') replaces منذ.

live.fut.why: MSA has a real future perfect: سأكون قد + past verb. People rarely say it; Levantine: بكون صرلي تلات سنين هون.

live.q.why: 'Since when' comes first, then a plain present verb. Levantine asks 'how much': قدّيش صرلك ساكن هون؟

if.real.why: إذا (idhaa) takes a past-form كان even for the future. Possession is عندي ('at me'), and فـ (fa) opens the result.

if.unreal.why: A different 'if', لو (law), marks it as imagined. The result is a past verb with the la- prefix: لسافرت, 'I would travel'.

if.past.why: Same لو clause as the imagined one. Adding كنت (kuntu) in the result moves it into the past: 'I would have travelled'.
